decision_conditions: Water Efficiency: Prior to first occupation for each building containing residential accommodation, a completed Water Efficiency Calculator for New Dwellings must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that internal potable water consumption for each of the dwellings will meet a target water use of 110 litres per person per day (l/p/d) based on the Government's national calculation method for water efficiency for the purposes of Part G of the Building Regulations. The Water Efficiency Calculator should be accompanied by details of the location and type of all appliances or fittings that use water, the capacity or flow rate of any equipment and any rainwater or greywater collection systems incorporated as part of the Development. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and the approved details shall be complied with for the life of the Development. Reason: To conserve water supplies in an area of water stress, in accordance with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Hard and Soft Landscaping: Prior to the commencement of superstructure works within a Phase, full details of hard and soft landscaping shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All hard and soft landscaping and tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and to a reasonable standard in accordance with the relevant recommendations of appropriate British Standards (in particular, BS 3882: Specifications for Topsoil, Recommendations (2015) and BS 8545: Trees from Nursery to Independence in the Landscape, Recommendations (2014) or other recognised codes of good practice). The works shall be carried out prior to the occupation of the relevant phase of the Development or in accordance with the timetable agreed with the Local Planning Authority. Any tree(s) or plants that (within a period of five years after planting) are removed, die, or (in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority) are damaged or defective shall be replaced as soon as is reasonably practicable with others of a similar size/species/number as originally approved, unless the Local Planning Authority gives its consent to any variation.Reason: To ensure the provision, establishment and maintenance of a reasonable standard of landscape in accordance with the approved designs in accordance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018

Landscape Management Plan: Prior to the first occupation of each Phase, a landscaping management plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall set out how the planting in each Phase will be managed for a minimum of 2 years from practical completion of each Phase, to ensure full and successful establishment of plants and trees. Any tree(s) or plants that (within a period of five years after planting) are removed, die or (in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority) are damaged or defective, shall be replaced as soon as is reasonably practicable with the others of similar size/species/number as originally approved, unless the Local Planning Authority gives its consent to any variation. The plans shall identify all landscaped areas that will be under communal management. The planting shall be thereafter managed in accordance with the approved management plan. Reason: To ensure the provision, establishment and maintenance of a reasonable standard of landscape in accordance with the approved design, in line with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Wayfinding: Prior to occupation within each relevant Phase an overarching wayfinding strategy for that phase must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority detailing the design approach to wayfinding infrastructure to be delivered. Reason: In the interests of public safety, wayfinding and promoting active travel, in accordance with Policy T3 of the London Plan 2021.

Non-Road Mobile Machinery: All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) or net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, Site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on Site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, Site preparation and construction phases of the Development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/ Reason: In order to reduce the environmental impact of the construction and the impact on the amenities of neighbouring residents and to accord with Policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

No Antenna or Telecomms: No satellite antenna, apparatus or plant of any sort (including structures or plant in connection with the use of telecommunication systems or any electronic communications apparatus) shall be erected on the side or roof of any buildings unless and until details of their size and location have previously been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority. The relevant part of the Development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained. Reason: In the interest of visual amenity and to accord with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Considerate Contractor: The lead contractor of each relevant Phase shall be signed up to the Considerate Constructors Scheme (CCS) and its published Code of Considerate Practice, and the details of (i) the membership, (ii) contact details, (iii) working hours as stipulated under the Control of Pollution Act 1974, and (iv) Certificate of Compliance, shall be clearly displayed on the Site so that they can be easily read by passing members of the public, and those details shall thereafter be maintained on display throughout the duration of the works being carried out in that Phase. Reason: To mitigate the impact of construction work upon the levels of amenity that neighbouring and future occupiers should reasonably expect to enjoy and to ensure accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Protected Species Survey (Outline Application Area only): No development within a relevant Phase within the Outline Application Area hereby approved shall take place until all necessary updated protected species survey information for the relevant Phase, including: a) badger, b) reptile & amphibian, and; c) bat activity has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To protect and enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and ensuring existing legislation is followed.

Time LimitThe Development shall be commenced before the expiration of THREE YEARS from the date of this planning permission. Reason: To comply with Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, as amended.

Commencement Limit: Applications for approval of the Reserved Matters relating to the Development shall be submitted to the Local Planing Authority before the expiration of 15 YEARS from the date of this Decision Notice and shall be commenced before the expiration of 2 YEARS from the date the relevant Reserved Matters Application is approved. Reason: To comply with Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended by Section 51 of the Planning and Compulsory Purchase Act 2004).

Phasing Strategy for LCH Development:  Prior to commencement of the Development hereby approved (other than in relation to Phase 1 Enabling Works or Enabling works), a Phasing Strategy for the LCH Development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The LCH Development shall thereafter be implemented in accordance with the approved Phasing Strategy or any strategy subsequently agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To facilitate the orderly approach to the construction of the Development in accordance with Chapter 11 of the National Planning Policy Framework and to ensure that the planning permission is a phased planning permission which expressly provides for development to be carried out in phases for the purposes of the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulations 2010 (as amended).

Reserved Matters Specification: In relation to the Outline Application Area, approval of the details of the access, appearance, landscaping, layout and scale of the Development, shall be obtained from the Local Planning Authority in writing prior to the commencement of any development within each Phase (other than in relation to Enabling works). Each application for the approval of Reserved Matters shall contain the information and other details as specified in the Reserved Matters Specification at [Annex A] of this planning permission, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority.The Development shall be carried out in accordance with the Reserved Matters approvals Reason: As required by Section 92 of the Town and Country Planning Act as amended.

Reserved Matters Compliance: Reserved Matters applications for the Outline Application Area shall be submitted and prepared in accordance with the approved Parameter Plans, Design Code and Development Specification Statement and such further relevant plot specific parameters and principles as are referred to elsewhere in these conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority through the reserved matters approval. Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and to identify the Development Plots/Parcels to which Reserved Matters applications will need to be submitted and approved and to ensure the reserved matters are in accordance with relevant approved parameters and principles.

Detailed Applications Area Floorspace: The total quantum of built floorspace for the Detailed Application Area hereby approved shall be in accordance with the following details: o Life sciences floorspace (Class E (g)) - gross internal area of 33,482 square metres; o Learning Lab welcome and outreach centre (Class E/ Sui Generis) - gross internal area of 697 square metres; and, o Flexible Class E and/or Sui Generis amenities space (Class E and Sui Generis amenities) - gross internal area of 762 square metres. The use class E (g) life sciences floorspace hereby approved shall only be used for Life Sciences. The gross internal area cited in this condition excludes enclosed parking areas within buildings and roof top plant enclosures. Reason: To ensure the detailed scheme is carried out in accordance with the details submitted.

Development thresholds and delivery of floorspace types: The total quantum of built floorspace on the Outline Application Area provided on Development Parcels B, C and D of the development shall not exceed the following thresholds: o Up to 10,200 square metres [gross internal area] of Residential Accommodation (Use Class C3 and/or C4); o Up to 45,000 square metres [gross internal area] of Class E (g);o Up to 1,500 square metres [gross internal area] for manufacturing uses specific to the life sciences industry (Use Class B2)*; and, o Up to 800 square metres [gross internal area] of flexible Class E and/or Sui Generis uses (flexible non-residential uses). *Provided that the cumulative gross internal floorspace for lifescience use (Class E (g) and /or B2 Good Manufacturing Practice) across the LCH Development (Detailed Application Area plus the relevant part of the Outline Application Area) does not exceed 78,482 square metres [gross internal area]. The use class E (g) and B2 Life Sciences floorspace hereby approved shall only be used for Life Sciences. The gross internal area cited in this condition excludes enclosed parking areas within buildings and roof top plant enclosures. Reason: To ensure the Development is carried out in accordance with the parameters assessed pursuant to the Environmental Statement in relation to the Development.

Tree (Protection): Prior to the commencement of each relevant Phase of development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of the retained trees within that phase, in accordance with BS 5837:2012, including a tree protection plan(s) (TPP) and an arboricultural method statement (AMS) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Specific issues to be dealt with in the TPP and AMS: a) Location and installation of services/ utilities/ drainage. b) Methods of demolition within the root protection area (RPA as defined in BS 5837: 2012) of the retained trees. c) Details of construction within the RPA or that may impact on the retained trees. d) A full specification for the installation of boundary treatment works, including where these are within an RPA. e) a full specification for the construction of any roads, parking areas and driveways, including details of the no-dig specification and extent of the areas of the roads, parking areas and driveways to be constructed using a no-dig specification. Details shall include relevant sections through them.f) Detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing, where the installation of no-dig surfacing within Root Protection Areas is proposed, demonstrating that they can be accommodated where they meet with any adjacent building damp proof courses. g) A specification for protective fencing to safeguard trees during both demolition and construction phases and a plan indicating the alignment of the protective fencing. h) A specification for scaffolding and ground protection within tree protection zones. i) Tree protection during construction indicated on a TPP and construction and construction activities clearly identified as prohibited in this area. j) Details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and use of fires. k) Methodology and detailed assessment of root pruning. l) Arboricultural supervision and inspection by a suitably qualified tree specialist. m) Reporting of inspection and supervision. The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details. Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the tree (s) to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality with best practice and Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Trees (Supervision): Before any development or construction work begins within each relevant Phase, a pre-commencement meeting shall be held on site and attended by the developers appointed arboricultural consultant, the site manager/foreman and a representative from the Local Planning Authority (LPA) to discuss details of the working procedures and agree either the precise position of the approved tree protection measures to be installed OR that all tree protection measures have been installed in accordance with the approved tree protection plan. The development shall thereafter be carried out in accordance with the approved details or any variation as may subsequently be agreed in writing by the LPA. Reason: Required prior to the commencement of development in order that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during development works and to ensure that, as far as is possible, the work is carried out in accordance with the approved details pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 in accordance with best practice and Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Lighting Strategy: No occupation/use of the relevant Phase or part thereof, hereby approved shall take place until a lighting scheme, including security lighting and the illumination of the buildings at night, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme shall include: i. functions of proposed lighting and the uses it supports e.g., for recreation facilities; ii. a lux plan showing both proposed and existing retained light sources; iii. details of time limits on lighting and hours of operation; iv. details of how the lighting scheme will mitigate any potential biodiversity impacts arising from the installation or operation of the proposed lighting; v. technical details of luminaries, fixtures, any supporting structures and systems of control such as timers and sensors including surface finish and colour and specifically explain what design attributes have been chosen to minimise light pollution; and vi. details on colour temperature of the lighting and the associated public realm surfaces including reflectivity and glare. The relevant Phase or part thereof shall not be occupied until the approved lighting scheme has been implemented in accordance with teh approved details, and thereafter lighting detailed in the approved scheme shall be retained for the lifetime of the development. The Lighting will be designed and installed to minimise impacts on biodiversity, as outlined in Guidance Note 08/23 Bats and Artificial Lighting (Institute of Lighting Professionals and the Bat Conservation Trust). Reason: To ensure there is an appropriate level of residential amenity and appropriate features to conserve and enhance the amenity of neighbours and wildlife habitats in accordance with Policy 29 of the Local Plan and to protect the biodiversity value of the remaining allotment land and adjacent land, in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Car Parking Design and Management Plan: a) A Site Wide Car Parking Design and Management Plan (CPDMP) for the LCH Development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to commencement of superstructure works. The Site Wide CPDMP shall set out the key principles that will guide parking management across the LCH Development and the long-term strategy for allocating, managing and monitoring on-Site parking including parking for blue badge and electric vehicles. The Site Wide CPDMP will include measures of how parking within the LCH Development will be minimised and provided only where necessary. b) Prior to the commencement of superstructure works on the LCH Development within each relevant Phase, a Phase Specific Car Parking Design and Management Plan (CPDMP) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Phase Specific CPDMP shall set out the strategy for implementing the Site Wide CPDMP within the relevant Phase, and shall identify the parking provision to be delivered with each building. Once the Phase Specific CPDMP is approved the car parking areas relating to each building shall be constructed and marked out prior to the first occupation of the building to which they relate, and thereafter retained permanently for the accommodation of vehicles of occupiers to the premises and not used for any other purpose. Blue badge car parking spaces shall be constructed and marked out as accessible parking bays prior to the first occupation of the building to which they relate and retained thereafter.Reason: To ensure that parking is appropriately managed and not to prejudice the free flow of traffic or conditions of general safety along the adjoining highway and to ensure and promote easier access for disabled persons, in accordance with Policies 36 and 37 of Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy T6 of the London Plan 2021.

Demolition and Construction Logistics Plan: Prior to the commencement of development within each Phase, a Construction Logistics Plan (CLP) for the Phase shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in writing. The CLP must include details of: (a) loading and unloading of plant and materials, (b) storage of plant and materials, (c) programme of works (including measures for traffic management), (d) hours of operation, (e) means to prevent deposition of mud on the highway, (f) delivery times (particularly abnormal loads), (g) holding areas, (h) contractors parking, (i) a Stage 1 Road Safety Audit in respect of any temporary works proposed at the junction of Brighton Road / Cotswold Road/ Chiltern Avenue to facilitate construction traffic movements, and, (j) how the developer/contractor will ensure Heavy Goods Vehicle construction movements only take place between 09:30 and 15:00 during school term time The development shall be constructed and implemented in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not interfere with the free flow of traffic and conditions of safety on the public highway, and does not have a significant adverse impact on the amenities of nearby residential properties and the nearby Harris Academy in accordance with Policies 29 and 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy T7 of the London Plan 2021. This is required to be pre-Commencement to mitigate against the impacts of the demolition and construction processes.

Demolition and Construction Environmental Management Plan: Prior to the commencement of development within each Phase, a Construction Environmental Management Plan (CEMP) must be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in writing. The CEMP shall be in accordance with BS42020:2013 and must include details of: a) Provision of boundary hoarding;b) Hours of operation; c) Means to control dust and emissions to air; d) Means to control noise and vibration; e) The qualifications, role and responsibilities of the appointed on site Ecological Clerk of Works. f) f) responsible persons and lines of communication to deliver the CEMP; g) g) risk assessment of potentially damaging construction activities; h) identification of 'biodiversity protection zones' and the practical measures (both physical measures and sensitive working practices) to avoid or reduce impacts during construction; i) the location and seasonal timing of works to avoid affecting birds and other fauna, as necessary if this is within the breeding season and the submission of any necessary surveys for nesting birds prior to works being undertaken; j) the times during construction when a specialist ecologist needs to be present on site to oversee works; k) measures to prevent entrapment of mammals; l) measures to eradicate invasive non-native plant species (Buddleja and cherry laurel etc.); m) construction lighting to ensure it is in accordance with Guidance Note 08/23 Bats and Artificial Lighting (Institute of Lighting Professionals and the Bat Conservation Trust). The CEMP should be in accordance with the GLA's Supplementary Planning Guidance 'Control of Dust and Emissions during Demolition and Construction'. All works carried out during the construction periods shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved CEMP. Reason: To ensure that the proposed Development does not have a significant adverse impact on the amenities of nearby residential properties, and receptors sensitive to vibration and noise e.g. MRI scanners and sensitive equipment in the wider LCD; future occupiers of the Residential Accommodation and to minimise the impacts on local air quality, and to enhance and protect the biodiversity value of the land. This condition is required to be pre-Commencement as the CEMP needs to be in place before any works take place and to mitigate against the impacts of the demolition and construction processes, including to ensure that protected species and the biodiversity value of the land are not harmed / mitigated prior to the demolition / construction process in accordance with Policies 26, 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Thames Water (Upgrades to foul water network): Each relevant building of development within the Outline Application Area shall not be occupied until confirmation is provided that either: 1. There is sufficient capacity within the foul water network to accommodate additional flows for the relevant building; or, 2. All necessary upgrades to the foul water network to accommodate additional flows from the relevant building have been completed; or 3. A phasing plan for development and infrastructure, agreed with Thames Water and the Local Planning Authority, is in place. Where such a plan exists, no occupation shall occur other than in accordance with the approved phasing schedule. Reason: Network reinforcement is likely to be required to support the proposed development. These upgrades are essential to avoid the risk of sewer flooding and pollution incidents.

Biodiversity Gain Plan and Habitat Management Plan: The relevant Phase of development hereby permitted, excluding Phase 1 Enabling Works and Enabling Works, may not commence until a Biodiversity Gain Plan (BGP) and Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP) for that phase has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved HMMP shall be implemented in full for its duration and shall contain the following full information on: 1) Green infrastructure, including but not limited to: i) Biodiverse / biosolar / intensive roofs, including how access for management & monitoring will be created and maintained;ii) Biodiverse roofs on bike / bin storage areas; iii) Ground based soft landscaping (including living walls, rain gardens etc.); iv) Planters. 2) A soft landscaping masterplan will detail biodiversity enhancement through planting schemes that provide nectar, pollen and fruit resources throughout the seasons, a variety of structural diversity and larval food plants, through no less than 60% native and local species by number and diversity. Substrate, provenance and numbers of all bulbs, seeds and plugs / whips / trees will be detailed, as will aftercare and ongoing management. Ornamental plants will not include any genera or species on Schedule 9 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act (1981) or the LISI list and should be on the "RHS Plants for Pollinators" lists (or of documented wildlife value), to provide increased resource availability. 3) Descriptions and prescriptions of the management operations necessary to achieve the aims and objectives; 4) Preparation of a works schedule, including when habitat creation will take place and an annual works schedule; 5) Details of the monitoring needed to measure the effectiveness of management; 6) Details of the timetable for each element of the monitoring programme; 7) Details of the person(s) responsible for the implementation of the management actions and monitoring; 8) Mechanisms of adaptive management to account for necessary changes in work schedule to achieve the required targets; 9) A timetable for review of the management actions and monitoring; and; 10) Reporting in years 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15, 20, 22, 25 and 30 after the creation of each habitat, with biodiversity reconciliation calculations at each stage (using the Statutory Metric & Condition Assessment sheets or updated versions), to be provided to the LPA no later than 1 November of each reporting period. Work shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme and thereafter retained in perpetuity. Reason: To deliver the legally-binding 10% biodiversity net gain, in accordance with Section 13 of the Environment Act 2021, as enacted in Section 90A of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended), as well as Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy G6 of the London Plan 2021.

Bat Survey (Outline Application Area only):Prior to the commencement of any works within a relevant Phase in the Outline Application Area, an updated Preliminary Roast Assessment (PRA) should be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. If any further surveys are required (such as Emergence), they must be undertaken and the report submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to any works taking place in that phase, or in accordance with a timetable to be agreed with the Local Planning Authority. If a bat roost is discovered on or off site that would be affected by the development and the works will be required to proceed under a European protected Species Licence (EPSL), prior to any licensable works being undertaken, the Local Planning Authority must be provided with: i) A copy of the licence issued by Natural England pursuant to Regulation 55 of the Conservation of Habitats and Species Regulations 2017 and the The Conservation of Habitats and Species (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019, authorising the specified activity/development to proceed, and; ii) A copy of all proposed bat mitigation and enhancement required to secure the necessary licence. Reason: To protect and enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and ensuring existing legislation is followed. This condition is required to be pre-commencement of demolition to the existing building and felling of any trees, to ensure that protected species are not harmed and, if necessary, fully mitigated for, prior to the modification / construction process through the granting of an appropriate licence.

Wildlife Features (Detailed Application Area only): Prior to commencement of superstructure works within each relevant Phase within the Detailed Application Area hereby approved, a scheme for wildlife and nesting features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These will include:a) Provision of connectivity for badger commuting and foraging areas, including badger gates within fences (as necessary); b) Hedgehog holes in new internal and boundary fencing and the provision of hedgehog homes in undisturbed areas of the site; c) Features for wildlife, in accord with the adopted Biodiversity Strategy, including at least (in total across the Detailed Application Area): i) 12no. integrated multi-chamber swift bricks, ii) 12no. integrated starling boxes, iii) 12no. integrated house sparrow terraces, iv) 12no. integrated bat boxes v) 12no. integrated bee bricks on sunny / south facing walls, vi) 5no. black redstart boxes on biodiverse roofs, The scheme will include full details on: numbers of each feature, type of feature / box / brick, location (plan and elevation views) of each feature, height above ground and location of nearby lighting. Features shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme and thereafter retained in perpetuity. Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Wildlife Features (Outline Application Area only): Prior to commencement of superstructure works within each relevant Phase within the Outline Application Area hereby approved, a scheme for wildlife and nesting features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These will include: a) Provision of connectivity for badger commuting and foraging areas, including badger gates within fences (as necessary); b) Hedgehog holes in new internal and boundary fencing and the provision of hedgehog homes in undisturbed areas of the site; c) Features for wildlife, in accord with the adopted Biodiversity Strategy, including at least (in total across Development Parcels B, C and D): i) 12no. integrated multi-chamber swift bricks, ii) 12no. integrated starling boxes, iii) 12no. integrated house sparrow terraces, iv) 12no. integrated bat boxes v) 12no. integrated bee bricks on sunny / south facing walls, vi) 5no. black redstart boxes on biodiverse roofs, The scheme will include full details on: numbers of each feature, type of feature / box / brick, location (plan and elevation views) of each feature, height above ground and location of nearby lighting. Features shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme and thereafter retained in perpetuity.Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Local Lead Flood Authority (Detailed Drainage Strategy): Prior to commencement of the groundworks within each relevant Phase (other than Phase 1 Enabling Works and Enabling works), a detailed drainage strategy that aligns with the approved drainage strategy [LCH-ARU-XX-XX-RP-D-00001], and supported by drainage calculations must be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Full drainage calculations should be modelled to include all areas that contribute to the drainage system (includingpermeable areas). Also, a detailed drainage layout which shows the location of all the proposed drainage components and the connectivity of the system to the point of discharge should be submitted. The layout must also show pipe numbers, gradients and pipe sizes, together with storage volumes of all SuDS components. Reason: To ensure the development is made safe without increasing flood risk elsewhere in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (Planning and flood risk) and associated guidance, policy SI13 of the London Plan 2021, and the National standards for sustainable drainage systems

Local Lead Flood Authority (Implementation and Management): No building in a relevant Phase hereby permitted shall be occupied, until evidence (e.g. photographs and installation contract) demonstrating that the sustainable drainage scheme for the relevant Phase has been completed in accordance with the approved details has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks and maintenance owner for all drainage components within each Phase must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components. Reason: To ensure the development is made safe without increasing flood risk elsewhere in accordance with the National Planning Policy Framework (Planning and flood risk) and associated guidance, policy SI13 of the London Plan 2021, and the National standards for sustainable drainage systems.

Thames Water (Piling Method Statement):No piling shall take place until a piling method statement (detailing the depth and type of piling to be undertaken and the methodology by which such piling will be carried out, including measures to prevent and minimise the potential for damage to subsurface sewerage infrastructure, and the programme for the works) and piling layout plan including all Thames Water wastewater assets, the local topography and clearance between the face of the pile to the face of a pipe has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority in consultation with Thames Water. Any piling must be undertaken in accordance with the terms of the approved piling method statement and piling layout plan. Reason: The proposed works will be in close proximity to underground sewerage utility infrastructure.

Environment Agency (Verification Report): Prior to occupation of the relevant Phase, a verification report demonstrating the completion of relevant works set out in the approved remediation strategy and the effectiveness of the remediation shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The report shall include results of sampling and monitoring carried out in accordance with the approved verification plan to demonstrate that the relevant site/phase remediation criteria have been met.Reason: To ensure that the site or relevant phase does not pose any further risk to human health or the water environment by demonstrating that the requirements of the approved verification plan have been met and that remediation of the relevant part of the site is complete. This is in line with paragraph 187 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Statement of Conformity: Prior to occupation of the last building within each relevant Phase, a Statement of Conformity shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Statement of Conformity is deemed the 'completion date' for the creation of all habitats set out within the relevant approved Biodiversity Gain Plan (BGP) and the Habitat Management and Monitoring Plan (HMMP). The Statement of Conformity will be signed by a Suitably Qualified Ecologist and include evidence in the form of full details on: a) Starting and completion dates for each 'significant onsite' habitat creation / Enhancement; b) Any limitations / impeding factors during each 'significant onsite' habitat creation / enhancement phase; c) Post completion photographs of each and every habitat / enhancement; d) Post installation photographs of each approved nesting / roosting feature e) proof will be provided that all natural environment data (e.g. habitats, species, green infrastructure features) from ecological surveys for the site (including pre and post-development), has been or can be shared with Greenspace Information for Greater London CIC (GiGL), London's environmental records centre, following GiGL's data standards (Item 10 of the BGP Template must be ticked at submission, unless there are overriding justifications provided for restricting information). Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Car Parking Provision (Detailed Application Area): Car Parking provision across the Detailed Application Area must not exceed a total of 134 car parking spaces (to include 6 disabled parking bays) for the Life Sciences, Learning Lab and Amenities uses. Reason: In the interest of promoting a modal shift to sustainable modes of transport in accordance with Policy 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018, and to ensure the Development is carried out in accordance with the parameters assessed pursuant to the Environmental Statement in relation to the Development.

Car Parking Provision: Car Parking provision across the development must not exceed a total of 300 car parking spaces (to include disabled parking provision).Reason: In the interest of promoting a modal shift to sustainable modes of transport in accordance with Policy 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018, and to ensure the Development is carried out in accordance with the parameters assessed pursuant to the Environmental Statement in relation to the Development

Cycle Parking:Before the first occupation of each relevant building, details (1:50 scale drawings) of the facilities to be provided for the secure storage of cycles and, where relevant, on-site changing facilities and showers for that building should be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The cycle parking for each building shall be constructed and fitted out in accordance with the approved details and the facilities, made available for use prior to occupation of the building to which the cycle parking relates and shall be retained for the life of the development. Reason: In order to ensure that satisfactory secure cycle parking and facilities for cyclists are provided and retained and in accordance with Policy T4 of the Local Plan 2021.

Solar Glare: Prior to the occupation of each relevant building in the Detailed Applications Area, where solar glare effects have been identified in the Environmental Statement (April 2025), and the Environmental Statement Addendum (December 2025), details shall be submitted to demonstrate that Solar Glare reflected from the facades of the building have been mitigated to safeguard amenity and minimise the potential for distraction of neighbouring road users. The approved measures shall be installed in accordance with the approved details and retained as such for the lifetime of the development. Reason: To safeguard the amenity of neighbouring residents and by reason of highway and pedestrian safety, in line with Policies D3, T1 and T2 of the London Plan (2021).

Materials: Prior to the commencement of superstructure works of each building, a schedule of materials and sample boards for all external facing materials to be used in the construction of that building shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. Mock-ups of facades shall be provided at a size to be agreed with the Local Planning Authority, on request. The development shall thereafter be constructed and retained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To secure high-quality design and detailing and to ensure that the appearance of the building and details achieves a high standard of design in accordance with LP Plan Policy D9 and SLP Policy 28 and 29

Delivery and Servicing Plan: A Site Wide Delivery and Servicing plan (DSP) for the LCH Development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to commencement of superstructure works. Prior to commencement of superstructure works for each building, a building specific Delivery and Servicing Plan (DSP) for the proposed uses shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The building specific DSP should provide details of the expected type and frequency of service vehicles including waste removal and for all uses, the hours within which they would arrive and depart, the intended locations for loading and unloading of vehicles and associated waiting and turning areas and access routes and show clear vehicle swept paths based on up to date information in relation to overall vehicle movements associated with the Development. The relevant building shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained. No residential building shall be occupied until the relevant Delivery and Servicing Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. No permitted use within any non-residential unit shall be commenced until the relevant Delivery and Servicing Plan for the relevant building has been submitted and approved. Reason: To ensure that vehicle movements associated with the use hereby permitted remains consistent and that the use shall not represent any unacceptable level, type, location or timing of vehicle movements such that the safety of pedestrians and cyclists and the efficiency of bus operations shall be unduly prejudiced, nor that residential amenity will be unduly affected.

Second Entrance: Details of a secondary pedestrian entrance to the Harris Academy Sixth Form shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval prior to the occupation of the first building within the Outline Application Area. The submission shall provide details of the proposed siting of the pedestrian entrance and any associated landscaping and boundary works to ensure appropriate access, together with a timetable for the delivery of the works. The new entrance shall be delivered and maintained in accordance with the approved details, and retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. Reason: In the interest of permeability and amenity of neighbouring occupants, in accordance with Policies D8 and T2 of the London Plan 2021.

Urban Greening Factor:Prior to commencement of superstructure works of each Phase within the Outline Application Area of the LCH Development, an Urban Greening Factor Statement must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate how the phase will contribute to a site-wide Urban Greening Factor target score of at least 0.3 using the Mayor of Lonodn's Methodology referenced in Policy G5 of the London Plan 2021. The approved urban greening measures set out shall thereafter be implemented and retained as such in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To comply with urban greening factor policy requirements in accordance with Policy G5 of the London Plan 2021.

Odours: Prior to first occupation of any non-residential unit hereby permitted with a commercial kitchen, details of any ventilation system for the removal and treatment of cooking odours from any commercial catering are to be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved details shall be fully implemented before the first use of the relevant non-residential unit and shall thereafter be permanently retained in an efficient manner. Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and minimise the impact of cooking smells, odours and noise, in accordance with Policies 28 and 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Noise Emissions: Prior to superstructure works commencing on each building containing residential accommodation, a scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the noise level of 35 dB LAeq,16 hour in living rooms and bedrooms during the daytime (0700 to 2300 hours) and 30 dB LAeq,8 hour during the night time (2300 to 0700 hours) in bedrooms, in accordance with BS8233:2014, shall not be exceeded. Noise levels in bedrooms should also not normally exceed 45 dB LAmax,F more than 10 times during the night time. Where these levels cannot be met with windows open appropriate acoustic ventilation should be provided so that the room can be sufficiently ventilated. The acoustic performance of any passive vent, variable speed mechanical air supply unit or whole house ventilation must be sufficient to ensure that the noise level standards given above are not compromised. Once agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority the approved details shall be installed prior to the relevant building being occupied and retained thereafter. Reason: To ensure that the proposed residential units are adequately protected from noise and to ensure an adequate level of internal amenity is provided for future residents, in accordance with Policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Plant Noise:Plants shall not be installed until measures to ensure that the rating level of any plant will be at least 5dBA lower than the existing background noise level at any given time of operation. The noise levels shall be measured or predicted 1m externally to any window at the nearest residential facade. Measurements and assessments shall be made in accordance with the BS 4142:2014. The development shall be carried out as approved. Reason: To ensure that the proposed and surrounding residential properties and other noise sensitive premises in the vicinity of Site are adequately protected from noise nuisance, in accordance with Policy 29 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Generators and Flues: Prior to the installation of any generators or flues relating to the life science use, details of the generators to be installed and drawings (roof plans and elevations) showing the siting, stack, height and diameter of the flue, together with a strategy for minimising air quality impacts, shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details. Reason: In the interests of protecting amenity and minimising the impacts of the development on air quality, in accordance with Policy SI1 of the London Plan 2021.

Public Open Space Management Plan: Prior to the occupation of each relevant Phase, a management plan for the public open space must be submitted to and approved in writing by teh Local Planning Authority. The plan for each relevant Phase of the Development shall set out how the public open space will be managed including its maintenance, in line with the principles set out in the Public London Charter LPG (or any relevant successor document). The public open space shall then be managed and maintained in accordance with the approved management plan, unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure appropriate management and maintenance arrangements are in place for the public open space, in accordance with Policies 25 and 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy D8 of the London Plan 2021.

Fire Statement: The development hereby approved within the Detailed Application Area shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Fire Statement prepared by Arup, dated April 2025. Reason: In the interests of fire safety and in accordance with Policy D5 and D12 of the London Plan 2021.

Energy Statement:The development hereby approved within the Detailed Application Area, shall be constructed in accordance with the details set out within the approved Energy Statement, prepared by Arup, dated December 2025. Reason: To ensure measures are implemented to reduce any detrimental environmental impact and to deliver an energy efficient and sustainable form of development in accordance with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI2 of the London Plan 2021.

Confirmatory Deed Pursuant to S106 Agreement: No development shall commence (other than Phase 1 Enabling Works and Enabling Works) until the applicant has entered into a Section 106 agreement, or where applicable, a confirmatory deed pursuant to Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990, in the form and on the terms approved under the Section 111 agreement entered into at the time of the grant of this planning permission. Written confirmation of completion of the Section 106 Agreement or confirmatory deed shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority prior to commencement. Reason: To secure the planning obligations necessary to make the development acceptable in planning terms, in accordance with Section 111 of the Local Government Act 1972 and Section 106 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 and relevant development plan policies.

Environment Agency (Site Investigation Scheme): No development approved by this planning permission shall commence within each relevant Phase until a strategy to deal with the potential risks associated with any contamination within that Phase has been submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority. This strategy will include the following components: 1. A site investigation scheme to provide information for a detailed assessment of the risk to all receptors that may be affected, including those off site. 2. The results of the site investigation and the detailed risk assessment referred to in (1) and, based on these, an options appraisal and remediation strategy giving full details of the remediation measures required and how they are to be undertaken. 3. A verification plan providing details of the data that will be collected in order to demonstrate that the works set out in the remediation strategy in (2) are complete and identifying any requirements for longer-term monitoring of pollutant linkages, maintenance and arrangements for contingency action. Any changes to these components require the written consent of the local planning authority. The scheme shall be implemented as approved. Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution in line with paragraph 187 of the National Planning Policy Framework.

Environment Agency (Contamination previously not identified): If, during development, contamination not previously identified is found to be present then no further development (unless otherwise agreed in writing with the Local Planning Authority) within the relevant Phase shall be carried out until a remediation strategy detailing how this contamination will be dealt with has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The remediation strategy shall be implemented as approved. Reason: To ensure that the development does not contribute to, or is not put at unacceptable risk from, or adversely affected by, unacceptable levels of water pollution from previously unidentified contamination sources at the development site in line with paragraph 187 of the National Planning Policy Framework and the aims and objectives of Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Metropolitan Police: The Development shall incorporate measures to design out crime and the relevant building shall not be occupied until secure by design accreditation for the relevant building has been achieved and evidence of such accreditation has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details. Reason: In pursuance of the Council's duty under section 17 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998 to consider crime and disorder implications in excising its planning functions; to promote the well-being of the area in pursuance of the Council's powers under section 2 of the Local Government Act 2000 and Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 which states that: The council will grant planning permission for new development, including new buildings, alterations and extensions, providing the new development: is secure and designed to minimise crime and anti-social behaviour. The development should provide a safe and secure environment in accordance with Policy D11 of the London Plan 2021.

London Fire Brigade (Fire Hydrant): Prior to occupation of each Phase, details of the location of any fire hydrants to be installed in that Phase shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval in writing. The fire hydrants shall thereafter be installed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To protect the safety and security of the occupants of the development in line with London Plan Policy D12 (2021).

Whole Life Carbon (Outline and Detailed Application Area): Prior to the occupation of each relevant building within each relevant Phase of the development, the post-construction tab of the GLA's Whole Life-Cycle Carbon Assessment template should be completed for the relevant phase having regard to the GLA's Whole Life Cycle Carbon Assessment Guidance, together with any supporting information, it should be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in writing. Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and to maximise the site carbon dioxide savings in compliance with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

BREEAM (Detailed Application Area):Within six month of occupation of each relevant building in the Detailed Application Area of the Development, a BREEAM New Construction V6.1 Post-Construction Certificate, issued by the BRE or equivalent authorizing body, must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that an 'Excellent' rating has been achieved for that building. All the measures integrated shall be retained for as long as the development is in existence. Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 31of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

BREEAM (Outline Application Area): Within six months of occupation of each relevant building within the Outline Application Area of the Development, a BREEAM New Construction V6.1 Post-Construction Certificate, issued by the BRE or equivalent authorizing body, must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that an 'Excellent' rating has been achieved for that building. All the measures integrated shall be retained for as long as the development is in existence. Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 31of the Sutton Local Plan 2018

Overheating (Detailed Application Area): a) The development hereby approved in the Detailed Application Area shall be constructed in accordance with the approved overheating strategy as set out in Section 7 of the approved Energy Strategy (Arup, December 2025) and in the TM52 Assessment included as Appendix A1 to the Energy Strategy. b) Prior to first occupation of each relevant building documentary evidence must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing which demonstrates that the overheating strategy has been implemented in accordance with the relevant approved details. Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 33 and London Plan Policy SI 4 2021.

Circular Economy:Prior to the occupation of each relevant building within within each phase of the development, a post construction monitoring report should be completed for the relevant phase having regard to the GLA's Circular Economy Statement Guidance. The report should be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority in writing. Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 33 2018 and London Plan Policy SI 4 2021.

description: A hybrid planning application (part full/part outline) comprising the following development which will be delivered in phases:In Full, carrying out of enabling works, erection of buildings providing lifescience and non-residential floorspace, cycle parking hubs and associated works including utilities, access, highways, landscaping and public realm works, provision of car and cycle parking and other works ancillary to the proposed development.In Outline, with all matters reserved: demolition of existing buildings and structures; erection of buildings providing lifescience floorspace, non-residential floorspace, and residential accommodation; partial removal and replacement of allotments; together with associated car and cycle parking, utilities, highways, access, landscaping and public realm works and other works ancillary to the proposed development.This application is accompanied by an Environmental Statement (ES) pursuant to the Town and Country Planning (Environmental Impact) Regulations 2017.
